title: Edges of inference — field scratchpad and reading takeaways
summary: Loose personal synthesis from a week of papers/blogs and a small internal brown-bag. Focus: practical heuristics for long-context inference (eviction, caching, sparse KV, and fallbacks). Not polished — questions for follow-up included.
notes:
Quick unordered notes:
- Practical problem: tail latency jumps when cache hit% drops below 60% for our 8k-serving config. Need better early-detection signals rather than averaging over minutes.
- Paper: 'Adaptive KV Eviction for Streaming Contexts' — idea: predict token reuse probability using short n-gram recency + client-level session features. Attractive because cheap to compute and incremental.
- Blog: rough anecdote about prefix-only caching failing with long-turn conversations that insert new topics mid-session — need lightweight recency detectors.
- Implementation thought: maintain per-session tiny sketch (LRU-ish but weighted by predicted reuse) -> only keep KV slices above threshold. Sketch size small (64 entries) keeps overhead low.
- Fallback design: when a shard is overloaded, rather than backoff entirely, route to quantized variant with warmed KV-less cold-start policy (synthesized prompt to reconstruct minimal context?). Still uneasy about quality loss.
- Measurement: instrument token-level path (cache-hit, cache-miss type, eviction reason, latency delta) and produce 95/99 pct histograms per model/region. Current observability is too coarse.
- Unresolved: how to correlate semantic importance with reuse heuristics (not only recency). Could embed sentence-level vectors and score reuse probability, but cost may outweigh value.
- Notes-to-self for experiment: A/B cache policy: baseline LRU vs predicted-reuse with per-session sketch. Metric: p95 generation latency, tokens/warm-minute, top-line quality via small prompt set (five queries).
- Edge-case: multi-user chat where a single user references many external docs -> KV blowup. Consider per-user soft quota + eviction by novelty score.
- SLO considerations: avoid synchronous eviction checks on critical path; make eviction async and bounded to avoid latency spikes.
- Rough timeline: spike a small PoC in Serving-Runtime sandbox next sprint (2 weeks) then run traffic shadow for a day.
- Discussion notes from brown-bag (Mira/Eliot): Mira suggested using RL-style reward shaping (cheap proxy reward = cache hit weighted by token-reuse) to tune eviction threshold offline. Eliot pushed back: risk of overfitting to synthetic traces. Good debate.
- To capture: create small synthetic workloads that simulate topic shifts mid-conversation (switch probability per 100 tokens) to stress test policies.
reading_list: Adaptive KV Eviction for Streaming Contexts — arXiv 2026 (notes: simple recency+session features; cheap)
Sketchy Caches: Compact Structures for Inference — SysML blog (2025) (notes: bloom-like weighting for KV retention)
Quantized Fallbacks and Quality Tradeoffs — internal draft (GH-PR-4700)
On the Cost of Semantic Repetition — workshop paper (ICML-WS 2024)
key_takeaways: Simple heuristics (recency + tiny session features) often capture most of the practical cache value — try cheap first.
Observability at token-path granularity is necessary to detect onset of cache-degradation before tail latency explodes.
Fallback strategies should prioritize graceful degradation (quantized models + minimal reconstruction) rather than outright failures.
Synthetic workloads that model topic shift are essential to tune eviction policies without risking prod regressions.
action_items: Draft a minimal sketch-based PoC design doc (Ben) — include API hooks for Runtime eviction and async sweeper.
Instrument token-path metrics in the sandbox (Eliot) — expose p95/p99 per model-route and cache-hit types.
Build synthetic topic-shift workload generator (Mira) — parameterize switch prob and external-doc frequency.
Schedule 30m sync with serving-runtime team to validate feasibility and perf budget (w/c 2026-09-20).
open_questions: 1) How much CPU/host memory overhead can we accept for per-session sketches before Dedicated customers push back? 2) Is semantic reuse estimation worth embedding-level cost? 3) How to gracefully degrade when both cache and fallback capacity are strained? 4) What privacy implications exist if sketches capture user doc ids? Need legal consult.
personal_reflections: I keep drifting between nicely elegant academic solutions (embeddings-driven reuse) and pragmatic low-cost heuristics. For product velocity, lean cheap-and-observable first; can layer more semantic-aware techniques later if we have clear failure cases. Stay mindful of SLO-first design.
